title: Reverse into a second buffer
starter:
%in  = buffer 5 dtype=i32 slot=0
%out = buffer 5 dtype=i32 slot=1
# out[i] = in[4 - i]. The starter copies without reversing.
%i   = range 5
%v   = shrink %in %i shape=[]
%x   = load %v
%o   = shrink %out %i shape=[]
%s   = store %o %x
%e   = end %s %i
%out1 = after %out %e
hints: There's no subtract op. How do you write 4 - i with add and mul?
`mul %i -1` then `add ... 4`. Use that as the offset into `%in`.
The bounds check works it out: i is in [0, 4], so -i is in [-4, 0], and 4 - i is in [0, 4].
explain: The source offset is `4 - i`, written as `add (mul %i -1) 4` on two lines. Interval arithmetic proves it lies in [0, 4], so the view of `%in` is in bounds without any masking.
